title: Change two shelf-edge price tickets in a clear ticket strip
instruction: Swap the middle and right cans' price tickets for the new ones from the stand; old tickets go in the waste tray.
context: O*NET 53-7065.00 Stockers and Order Fillers (about 2.8 million US workers) lists 'Stamp, attach, or change price tags on merchandise, referring to price list'. Most supermarket shelf edges carry clear PVC data strips: the 39 mm ticket stands in a channel behind a springy clear front that grips it. Changing one means getting the old ticket out and the new one to the bottom of the channel under the right product. What goes wrong: the new ticket ends crooked or half in and falls out, under the wrong product or in front of the old one, or a can is knocked down. It is physically hard because a seated ticket shows only a 9.5 mm strip of card against the strip's back, too little and too flat to pinch: with the springy front eased open the card must first be slid up by fingertip friction against the strip's back, then pinched, and the new 0.3 mm card must be dropped into a channel a few millimetres wide while the other hand keeps the front open.
setup: All real size; metres; x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +-0.305); station table top z = 0.7475. Shelf (fixed): a 400 mm section (y -0.20 to +0.20) of a steel gondola base shelf, 1.5 mm deck 370 mm deep with its top at z = 0.8675 (120 mm above the table), front flange 42 mm tall with its front face at x = 0.150, base plinth set back 15 mm. Ticket strip (taped to the flange, fixed): HL Display DBR datastrip, clear PVC, 39 mm label height (item 304622, 1000 mm, cut to 400 mm), 42 mm high, top flush with the deck. Profile: 1.0 mm back wall (front face x = 0.149); 1.0 mm channel to the 0.8 mm clear front, joined along a bottom fold whose floor is at z = 0.8285 (a seated ticket's top is flush with the back wall's top). The clear front is 29.5 mm tall, so a seated ticket's top 9.5 mm stands above it against the back wall; its top edge is rolled in to 0.2 mm from the back wall over z 0.8525-0.8560 and carries a 6 mm flat grip edge (z 0.8570-0.8580). The front springs shut on the tickets: it bends open along the bottom fold, 0.06 N m/rad, preloaded 10 deg (0.41 N at the rolled edge on the tickets; about 2 N on the grip edge holds it 30 deg open), opens to 36 deg; 13 g. Cans (free): three No. 300 food cans (76 x 113 mm, 15 oz net, 0.47 kg) standing on the deck at x = 0.298 (fronts 110 mm behind the strip): y = +0.06 sweetcorn (yellow label), -0.04 tomatoes (red), -0.14 peas (green). Tickets (free): white 300 gsm board, 0.3 mm thick, 60 wide x 39 high, 0.7 g, printed face toward the robot with a 52 x 16 mm band in its product's colour (name and price) 6 mm above the bottom edge. Three are seated in the strip, centred under the cans: centres (0.1489, y of the can, 0.8480), yellow, red (old price) and green (old price). Ticket stand (fixed, grey ABS): 50 x 72 x 15 mm, 4 mm floor, two 1.0 mm slots 64 mm long along y, 25 mm apart; centre (0.075, -0.175) on the table. The two new tickets stand in its slots, leaning on each slot's rear face, centres z = 0.7710, y = -0.175: green band (right can) in the front slot at x = 0.0629, red band (middle can) in the rear slot at x = 0.0879. Waste tray (fixed, grey ABS): 100 x 120 mm outside, 25 mm walls, 3 mm floor, centre (0.050, -0.050) on the table. Friction static/dynamic (estimates): tickets 0.8/0.7, strip 0.2/0.15, cans, shelf and tray 0.4/0.35, stand 0.3/0.25. Full dimension table and parts list: README.
scoring: End state, read when the run ends. A ticket is SEATED under a can when: its centre plane lies between the inside of the closed clear front and the back wall (1 mm allowance); its lowest corner is within 2 mm of the channel floor; it is upright (within 5 deg); its printed face points to the aisle (within 30 deg); its centre is within 15 mm, along the shelf, of that can's centre line; and the clear front is shut (within 2 deg of closed). For each of the middle and right cans: 0.25 when its old ticket is out of the strip and in the waste tray (centre inside the tray's inner walls, below the rim); a further 0.25 when its own new ticket is seated under it and its old ticket is no longer in the strip (a new ticket put in front of the old one earns nothing). Maximum 1.0. A new ticket under the other can earns nothing. Any credit needs all of: the left can's ticket still seated; both grippers released (each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from every ticket's bounding box); every ticket, every can and the clear front at rest (each moving less than 0.5 mm per 50 ms control step), all held for 1 s; held, hovering or still-moving states score 0. Permanent 0 for the rest of the trial (sticky, checked every step) if any can is ever tipped more than 20 deg or dropped 20 mm (off the shelf). Success = 1.0 held a further 1 s, which ends the trial. Real trial: after the robot lets go, a front photo with a ruler laid along the strip (centring, uprightness; a seated ticket's top is flush with the strip's back wall: check with a straightedge), a look that the clear front is shut and into the waste tray; release, stillness and the cans from the video.
run_limit: 4,800 steps (240 seconds at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at step 2,132 (107 s)
reset_notes: Seat the red-band and green-band old tickets back in the strip under the middle and right cans (the yellow one stays), stand the new tickets back in the stand (green front slot, red rear slot), cans back on their marks, waste tray empty, clear front shut.
fidelity: Tickets are rigid 0.3 mm cards (no bending or curling). The clear front is one rigid 400 mm piece hinged along its bottom fold with a torsion spring; its clear window collides but is not drawn (the renderer has no transparent material); a real PVC front is one springy extrusion that opens locally. Spring and friction values are estimates: measure the strip you use. The strip's tape is not modelled (fixed).
